newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on late liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on late liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates pared earlier increases to close unchanged at 23.50 percent on Friday following late demand, traders said.
"For most of the session you could see speculation by players who were liquid, but rates turned back down at the close as cash flowed in to the market," a trader said.
Traders said the U.S. bond market also exerted upside pressure on domestic rates during the session.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 21/32 to yield 7.17 percent.
Money market analysts said U.S. rates gained in the wake of strong sales and producer price data announced in early trade.

"Generally, conditions in Mexico are conducive to foreign investment, but right now the increase in U.S. interest rates forces up local rates in order to prevent an outflow of foreign capital," an analyst said.
"The U.S. long bond (yield) is what has thwarted the favorable trend rates could had," he added.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended down 20 basis points at 25.00 percent. Banco de Mexico drained 5.023
billion pesos from the market through four secondary auctions which it assigned at rates of between 25.27-25.41 percent.
Liquidity of 6.446 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
